A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BumbleBee research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison across the revised layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original IsaacGym and MuJoCo evaluations, clustering and delta-action ablations, and real-world Unitree G1 demonstrations, including Tables 1–6 and Figures 1 and 4–6.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulation and robot results, revises the reported demonstration duration, and adds confidence intervals in Appendix D, Table 12.

M1.justification: The AE clustering, cluster-specific tracking and delta-action experts, iterative refinement, and Transformer generalist distilled with DAgger remain unchanged. The objectives, reward designs, and architectures also match.

E1.justification: Both versions use filtered AMASS motions, HumanML3D annotations, IsaacGym, MuJoCo, and the Unitree G1. Boxing and Charleston demonstrations already appear in v1; the longer duration reported in v3 extends existing task coverage.

E2.justification: OmniH2O, Exbody2, and Hover remain the evaluated external baselines. General Init, Random, and the specialized/general delta-model comparison variants are also retained. Table 12 repeats the existing comparator set.

E3.justification: Figure 1 changes the reported real-world demonstration duration from 34.78 seconds to 135 seconds, including a full Charleston dance. The simulation protocols, robot configuration, termination thresholds, and training settings remain unchanged. The added metric descriptions do not establish that existing evaluations were recomputed.

E4.justification: Figure 1 revises the sustained real-world tracking case to report a longer boxing/Charleston sequence. The clustering ablations, iterative-refinement analysis, general-versus-specialized delta-model comparison, and Appendix D cluster-wise analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without confidence intervals. v3 introduces confidence intervals for all methods and metrics in the primary two-simulator comparison through Table 12. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting, although the caption specifies samples on a single reference trajectory and leaves the confidence level, sample count, and interval construction unspecified; additional training runs are not established.

E6.justification: Existing quantitative results remain unchanged, including BB success rates of 89.58% in IsaacGym and 66.84% in MuJoCo. Table 12 adds confidence-interval values around the retained scores, while Figure 1 revises the demonstrated duration from approximately 35 to 135 seconds. These do not establish a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The clustering loss, distillation objective, and modified-dynamics equation are unchanged. Appendix A.3 supplies averaging formulas for existing error metrics as additional explanation; it introduces no new theoretical result, proof, or substantive mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: motion clustering, an expert-to-generalist framework, cluster-specific sim-to-real adaptation, and superior general whole-body control. The longer demonstration and added reporting support existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 adds a substantive limitation that pipeline complexity constrains scalability, particularly when incorporating real-world training feedback. The localization limitation and explanations of specialization, iterative refinement, and generalist performance are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.3 documents success criteria, error formulas, and measurement units where v1 supplied only brief main-text descriptions. Its MPJPE wording remains ambiguous because it describes three-dimensional joint positions while specifying radians. Implementation settings, hardware, rollout collection, and code links otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to prior whole-body controllers and ASAP are retained. Switching from author-year citations to numbered references and changing bibliographic formatting do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and narrative order are retained. v3 groups retargeting and AE clustering under Dataset Curation, adds the metric subsection and statistical-reporting paragraph, updates author credits, and corrects 'Run' to 'Walk-fast' in the Table 6 discussion.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a document-wide visual redesign with wider text blocks, changed typography, a branded title page, and a shaded abstract spanning two pages. Figures and tables are resized or repositioned, Figure 4's swapped Jump/Stand Low captions are corrected, Figure 1 is updated, and Table 12 is added.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects Figure 4's swapped labels, acknowledges a concrete scalability limitation, and adds evaluation definitions and uncertainty reporting absent from v1. These improve interpretation and documentation. The gains remain limited because Table 12 omits confidence-level and sample-count information, Appendix A.3 ambiguously combines three-dimensional joint positions with angular units, and the main quantitative evidence is unchanged.
